en.title: Our 7 Favorite 2000s Movie Villains — Get Ready to Shudder
en.summary: The 2000s gave us heroes, but the villains were truly unforgettable. From chilling psychopaths to existential threats, these bad guys defined a decade of cinema.
en.body:
## 1. Anton Chigurh (No Country for Old Men, 2007)
This relentless force of nature, brought to chilling life by Javier Bardem, embodies an unstoppable, almost cosmic, evil. Chigurh isn't driven by greed or revenge, but by a terrifyingly simple, fatalistic philosophy, making his coin-toss decisions and brutal efficiency all the more unsettling.

## 2. The Joker (The Dark Knight, 2008)
Heath Ledger's Oscar-winning portrayal of Batman's arch-nemesis wasn't just a performance; it was a phenomenon. This Joker is pure, anarchic chaos, a philosophical terrorist who wants to watch the world burn, proving that sometimes the greatest villain is one who believes in nothing.

## 3. Hans Landa (Inglourious Basterds, 2009)
Christoph Waltz’s "Jew Hunter" is a masterclass in sophisticated villainy. Landa is terrifyingly charming, intelligent, and utterly ruthless, a linguistic chameleon who can switch from polite interrogation to chilling menace in an instant, making him one of Tarantino’s most memorable creations.

## 4. Voldemort (Harry Potter Franchise, 2001-2011)
Lord Voldemort is the embodiment of pure evil and the ultimate antagonist to Harry Potter. His quest for immortality and power, coupled with his spectral presence and terrifying magic, made him the boogeyman for a generation and a constant, looming threat throughout the entire saga.

## 5. Killmonger (Black Panther, 2018)
Michael B. Jordan's Erik Killmonger is more than just a villain; he's a compelling anti-hero with a righteous, albeit extreme, agenda. His critique of Wakanda's isolationism and his vision for global upheaval resonate deeply, making his motivations understandable even as his methods are horrifying.

## 6. Jigsaw (Saw Franchise, 2004-2010)
John Kramer, aka Jigsaw, redefined the horror villain with his elaborate, morally ambiguous traps. His "games" were designed to test the will to live, forcing victims into impossible choices and leaving a legacy of gruesome puzzles that haunted audiences throughout the decade.

## 7. Hannibal Lecter (Hannibal Rising, 2007)
While Hannibal Lecter's iconic status was cemented in the 90s, his origin story in *Hannibal Rising* offered a chilling glimpse into the making of the cannibalistic genius. Gaspard Ulliel’s portrayal explored the trauma that shaped Lecter into the sophisticated, terrifying serial killer he would become.

Bottom Line: The 2000s proved that the best villains are often the most complex, leaving an indelible mark on cinematic history.

content_raw: As the world said goodbye to the 1990s and welcomed in a new decade, a new century, and a new millennium, the cinematic world thrived. Some of the great franchises of the '90s continued through the 2000s, as well as new ones establishing themselves, with some of the greatest movies of all time debuting across this new ten-year stretch. The noughties gave the world iconic heroes, the likes of a new and soon-to-be longest reigning James Bond ever, a new era of superhero movies that would change the game forever, and more than a few powerful wizards. But what of the villains that faced such icons? As much as they so often take the spotlight, there wouldn't be much of a story to tell without a struggle for the protagonist, an obstacle for them to overcome, or an equally brilliant adversary to lock horns with, and the 2000s had such bad guys to spare. Inventive serial killers, terrorists, heroes gone bad, corrupt cops, gang leaders, and even famous cannibals helped make some of the decade's best outings so great, and graced even weak or underwhelming films as some of their brightest lights. Yes, this was a good decade to be bad.
